proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
The capped clipped-ramp construction makes every \(Y_{nt}^\sigma(a)\) deterministic under the assignment law, so the finite-population fixed-outcome condition holds. Since \(0\le g(u)\le M\),
\[
 |Y_{nt}^\sigma(0)|=0,
 \qquad
 |Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)|=g(t/n)\le M,
\]
which verifies outcome boundedness. The construction specifies
\(\Pr_\sigma(A_{nt}=1\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=e_{nt}\), and, because \(c>0\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\),
\[
 0<e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,c/t\}\le\rho<1.
\]
Thus the predictable assignment-law and propensity-range conditions hold. The two regressions are identically zero, hence are \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\)-measurable and satisfy \(|m_{nt}(a)|=0\le M_m\). This proves the predictable- and bounded-regression conditions.

The constructed intensity is \(\bar q^\sigma(u)=c\). Therefore \(\bar q^\sigma(0)=c\),
\[
 c/2\le \bar q^\sigma(u)=c\le K,
 \qquad
 |\bar q^\sigma(u)-\bar q^\sigma(v)|=0\le L_q|u-v|.
\]
By the definition of \(\mathcal Q\), these three displayed facts give \(\bar q^\sigma\in\mathcal Q\). The map \(u\mapsto(u-a_\star)_+\) is one-Lipschitz, multiplication by \(L_r\) gives Lipschitz modulus \(L_r\), and truncation by the constant \(M\) is nonexpansive. Since \(B=M+M_m\ge M\), it follows that
\[
 |r^\sigma(u)|=g(u)\le M\le B,
 \qquad
 |r^\sigma(u)-r^\sigma(v)|\le L_r|u-v|.
\]
The definition of \(\mathcal R\) now yields \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\).

It remains to establish the asserted eventual good-event statement from the construction. The conditions \(n\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), \(\varepsilon_n\to0\), and \(a_\star>0\) imply that there is an integer \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
 \lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil>c/\rho,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_n+1/n<a_\star,
 \qquad
 \lfloor a_\star n\rfloor+1>c/\rho.
\]
Indeed, the first inequality follows from \(n\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), the second from \(\varepsilon_n+1/n\to0\), and the third from \(a_\star n\to\infty\). If \(n\ge N\) and \(t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\), then \(t>c/\rho\), so \(c/t<\rho\) and
\[
 e_{nt}=c/t,
 \qquad
 t e_{nt}=c=\bar q^\sigma(t/n).
\]
The same cap-inactivity conclusion holds whenever \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\), by the third inequality. Moreover, for every \(t\),
\[
 r_{nt}(1)=Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)-m_{nt}(1)
 =r^\sigma(t/n),
\]
so the residual-profile discrepancy is identically zero.

For an early index \(t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\),
\[
 \frac tn<\frac{\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil}{n}
 \le\varepsilon_n+\frac1n<a_\star.
\]
Consequently \(r_{nt}(1)=0\). Every summand in
\[
 S_{n,\mathrm{rare}}^{\mathrm{early}}
 =\frac1n\sum_{t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil}
 (A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{r_{nt}(1)}{e_{nt}}
\]
is zero; hence this term is identically zero and its predictable quadratic variation is \(0\le v_{0,n}\). All three clauses in the definition of \(G_n\) therefore hold on the whole sample space for every \(n\ge N\), proving \(G_n=\Omega\) eventually.

This last conclusion is not an every-\(n\) profile-contract certificate. At a finite retained index \(t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\) for which \(c/t>\rho\), the cap gives
\[
 |t e_{nt}-\bar q^\sigma(t/n)|=c-t\rho.
\]
If \(\delta_{q,n}<c-t\rho\), the intensity clause of \(G_n\) fails. Thus eventual cap inactivity proves exactly the eventual assertion above, but it cannot by itself prove the contract required for every \(n\).

Let
\[
 \phi_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}.
\]
We first certify the residual optimization. Consider any two-sign late-void witness with profiles \(\widetilde r^+=g\) and \(\widetilde r^-=-g\), where \(g=0\) on \([0,a]\), \(|g(u)|\le M\), and \(g\) has Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\). Since \(g(a)=0\), Lipschitz continuity gives, for \(u>a\),
\[
 |g(u)|=|g(u)-g(a)|\le L_r(u-a).
\]
Combining this inequality with \(|g(u)|\le M\), and using \(g(u)=0\) for \(u\le a\), yields the pointwise certificate
\[
 |g(u)|\le\phi_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}.
\]
The capped clipped ramp attains equality everywhere. Therefore every such witness obeys
\[
 \left|2\int_0^1 g(u)\,du\right|
 \le 2\int_a^1\phi_a(u)\,du
 =2\int_0^{1-a}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =d(1-a),
\]
where direct integration gives
\[
 d(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]

The function \(d\) is continuous on \([0,1]\), and it is strictly increasing because
\[
 d(y)-d(x)=2\int_x^y\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds>0
 \quad\text{whenever }0\le x<y\le1.
\]
Its endpoint value is
\[
 d(1)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
 =d_{\max}.
\]
If \(L_r\le M\), then \(M^2/L_r\ge d_{\max}\), so every \(d\in(0,d_{\max})\) is on the quadratic branch and \(x(d)=\sqrt{d/L_r}\). If \(L_r>M\), the clipping point \(x=M/L_r\) lies in \((0,1)\), its image is \(M^2/L_r\), and inversion of the two branches gives exactly
\[
 x(d)=
 \begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus, in all cases,
\[
 x(d)\in(0,1),\qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),
 \qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]
The clipping elbow is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\).

Fix \(d\in(0,d_{\max})\), select the capped clipped-ramp pair with \(a_\star=a(d)\), and let \(\gamma_n\) be its maximum miscoverage probability as defined in the statement. The selected-pair premise is
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
The established sharp two-sign clipped-ramp theorem gives, for both \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n-2\gamma_n]_+,
 \qquad
 \eta_n\longrightarrow a(d)^c,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n\ge d(1-a(d))=d.
\]
Since \(\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}\subseteq
\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}\), for every \(\epsilon>0\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy
\[
 \eta_n\ge a(d)^c-\epsilon,
 \qquad
 \gamma_n\le\alpha+\epsilon.
\]
Monotonicity of the positive-part map then gives
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[a(d)^c-2\alpha-3\epsilon]_+.
\]
Taking the lower limit and then letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), using continuity of \(x\mapsto[x]_+\), proves
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[a(d)^c-2\alpha]_+
 =[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
No structured-class inclusion is used in this implication.

For completeness, the sharp theorem's pairwise attainment can be seen directly. Put \(m_n=\lfloor a(d)n\rfloor\) and let
\[
 V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^n\{A_{nt}=0\}.
\]
Under either sign, \(\Pr_\sigma(V_n)=\eta_n\). On \(V_n\), all pre-ramp treated outcomes are zero and no post-ramp treatment is observed, so the complete logged observation has the same value under the two signs. On \(V_n^c\), some \(t>m_n\) is treated and \(Y_{nt}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\sigma\phi_{a(d)}(t/n)\ne0\), so the sign is revealed. If \(\eta_n>2\alpha\), use an independent uniform randomizer on \(V_n\) to report \(\{\tau_n^+,\tau_n^-\}\) with probability \(1-2\alpha/\eta_n\), and each singleton with probability \(\alpha/\eta_n\); on \(V_n^c\), report the revealed true singleton. Each sign then has miscoverage exactly \(\alpha\), and
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 =\eta_n-2\alpha.
\]
If \(\eta_n\le2\alpha\), report either singleton with probability one half on \(V_n\), and again report the revealed singleton on \(V_n^c\). Each sign then has miscoverage \(\eta_n/2\le\alpha\), and the probability of diameter at least \(\Delta_n\) is zero. Thus in both cases it equals \([\eta_n-2\alpha]_+\). The only positive-diameter report in this construction is the two-target set, whose diameter is \(\Delta_n\ge d\); hence
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 =[\eta_n-2\alpha]_+
 \longrightarrow[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
This is attainment within the selected pair, not a globally attaining confidence procedure.

Finally, let another admissible late-void pair start at \(a'=1-x'\) and have limiting causal separation at least \(d\). The pointwise certificate above implies \(d\le d(x')\). Strict monotonicity of \(d\) forces \(x'\ge x(d)\), and therefore its constant-intensity limiting void mass satisfies
\[
 (a')^c=(1-x')^c\le(1-x(d))^c.
\]
This is the matching optimality certificate for the claimed late-void envelope.

As an exact boundary check, specialize to \(c=a_\star=1/2\), \(L_r=1/2\), \(M\ge1/4\), and choose \(\rho\ge1/2\). Then
\[
 d(1/2)=1/8,
 \qquad
 [(1/2)^{1/2}-2(0.05)]_+
 =0.6071067811865475\ldots.
\]
For \(n=1,2,3,4\), the post-ramp factor sets are respectively \(\{1\}\), \(\{2\}\), \(\{2,3\}\), and \(\{3,4\}\). Because the cap is inactive on those factors when \(\rho\ge1/2\), direct multiplication gives
\[
 \eta_1=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \eta_2=\frac34,
 \qquad
 \eta_3=\frac58,
 \qquad
 \eta_4=\frac{35}{48}.
\]
The cap qualification is necessary: if \(\rho<1/2\), then \(\eta_1=1-\rho\), so these four diagnostic values are not claimed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Every member of the capped clipped-ramp family satisfies the declared fixed-outcome, outcome-boundedness, predictable-randomization, propensity-range, predictable-regression, bounded-regression, intensity-profile, and residual-profile conditions. In particular, \(\bar q^\sigma\in\mathcal Q\) and \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every time after the profile cutoff and also at every time after the late-ramp start, both profile discrepancies in \(G_n\) are zero, the early rare-arm term and its predictable quadratic variation are zero, and hence \(G_n=\Omega\). These conclusions are eventual: they do not establish the profile-contract condition for every \(n\), and therefore do not by themselves certify membership in the full structured class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The construction proves the profile event only eventually. At an included finite index where the propensity cap is active, the logged intensity discrepancy can exceed the supplied tolerance, so eventual exactness cannot certify the every-n profile contract or full structured-class membership.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume \(L_r>0\), and define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
For every \(d\) with \(0<d<d_{\max}\), set
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d).
\]
Select the capped clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)\), and define
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
If the selected pair satisfies \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha\), then, under each sign,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
The elbow \(d=M^2/L_r\) is interior to \((0,d_{\max})\) exactly when \(L_r>M\). Among two-sign late-void witnesses whose residual profiles vanish on \([0,a]\), are bounded in absolute value by \(M\), and have Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\), the clipped profile is pointwise optimal, and the displayed bound is the optimized late-void envelope. For each selected two-sign clipped-ramp subexperiment the bound is attained asymptotically by an exact randomized allocation, but no global minimax attainment over the full structured class is claimed. Uniform honesty over a larger class is sufficient only if that selected pair is separately known to belong to the larger class for every \(n\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Uniform honesty over the declared structured class does not imply honesty for a capped pair that has only eventual, rather than every-n, profile-contract membership. The exact finite common-void inequality needs only the selected-pair miscoverage premise, which yields the same residual-optimized envelope and pairwise attainment.

proposed.statement: Every member of the capped clipped-ramp family satisfies the declared fixed-outcome, outcome-boundedness, predictable-randomization, propensity-range, predictable-regression, bounded-regression, intensity-profile, and residual-profile conditions. In particular, \(\bar q^\sigma\in\mathcal Q\) and \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every time after the profile cutoff and also at every time after the late-ramp start, both profile discrepancies in \(G_n\) are zero, the early rare-arm term and its predictable quadratic variation are zero, and hence \(G_n=\Omega\). These conclusions are eventual: they do not establish the profile-contract condition for every \(n\), and therefore do not by themselves certify membership in the full structured class.
proposed.justification: This proposition verifies the fixed, bounded, predictable, and profile-shape facts supplied by the capped construction, together with eventual exactness of its profile event, without promoting eventual exactness to an every-n class-membership certificate.
proposed.gap: At a finite profile-controlled index the propensity cap can force a logged-intensity discrepancy larger than the supplied tolerance, so the all-n profile contract requires a separate argument.
proposed.consumer: The sharp constant-intensity pair theorem uses these construction facts; any larger-class transfer must establish its own every-n inclusion or pair-honesty premise.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the all-n profile-contract dependency and record the eventual-only scope in the complete statement post-image.

prose_updates.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's original structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the retained constant-intensity clipped-ramp theorem optimizes the residual late-void obstruction under honesty for the selected pair; its eventual profile exactness is not an unconditional structured-class converse. A distinct pointwise-minimal intensity \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) yields the jointly optimized pair-honesty envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\), with residual and intensity elbows that may occur in either order. Direct every-\(n\) inclusion transfers the converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. Exact attainment is pairwise only. The exact \(1/8\), \(0.60710678\), directed \(13/32\), and high-hazard \(0.442M\) results remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor jointly optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction. Moreover, eventual disappearance of an early propensity cap does not imply the every-\(n\) profile contract needed to turn either selected capped witness into an unconditional structured-class converse.
project_justification.niche: The boundary has distinct positive and converse deliverables. Structured deterministic profiles with the supplied every-\(n\) contract support computable atom-safe calibration. For information limits, the constant-intensity clipped ramp optimizes residual separation under selected-pair honesty, while \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) is pointwise minimal in \(\mathcal Q\) and maximizes late-void mass for each fixed start. Combining the latter intensity with the clipped residual gives a separate pair-honesty frontier with both intensity and residual elbows.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the original structured subclass, the exact constant-intensity clipped-ramp pair tradeoff, and a separate exact intensity-optimized two-sign tradeoff. Both optimized asymptotic envelopes are stated under honesty for the selected pair because the corresponding membership certificates guarantee \(G_n=\Omega\) only eventually, not the profile contract for every \(n\). Direct every-\(n\) inclusion arguments transfer converse conclusions to Li and Zhao's baseline class; pairwise attainment and positive calibration retain their separate scopes.

prose_updates.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains both the constant-intensity clipped ramps and the separate intensity-optimized arrays for every \(n\), but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; both bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The selected-pair late-void converses and their direct baseline-class transfers are logically separate from this note's structured-class positive calibration. Only converse bounds transfer; matching confidence-set constructions remain sharp inside selected two-sign experiments. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024), Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026), and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) do not supply the present finite-population signed atomic calibration or jointly optimized common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply the all-estimator lower bounds. Those bounds instead use exact common subprobabilities on late-arm void events. For both the constant-intensity capped family and the separate intensity-optimized family, \(G_n=\Omega\) is proved only eventually: at a finite included index where the uncapped intensity divided by time exceeds \(\rho\), the intensity discrepancy can exceed \(\delta_{q,n}\). Their optimized frontiers therefore assume honesty on the selected pair rather than inferring it from full structured-class membership. A larger-class uniform-honesty premise is sufficient only after separate every-\(n\) inclusion is proved, as in the direct Li--Zhao baseline transfers. Both matching procedures know their selected pair, so neither establishes global minimax attainment. The positive theorem still requires its supplied profile and early-variation contracts, the \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound, and the polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because no polynomial bound controls profile boxes straddling the certification boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform finite-experiment coverage applies to the original bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with its supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. The constant-intensity envelope \([(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+\) and the stronger joint-intensity envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\) are selected-pair honesty conclusions: eventual \(G_n=\Omega\) does not by itself place either capped witness in the full structured class for every \(n\). Direct every-\(n\) baseline inclusion transfers the corresponding converses, but neither positive calibration nor attainment, to Li and Zhao's class. Exact attainment is confined to each selected two-sign pair; no global minimax procedure is claimed. The original linear-ramp frontier, exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) diagnostic with its \(\rho\ge1/2\) cap qualification, directed \(13/32\) certificate, and high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain valid. No polynomial certificate-complexity exponent is asserted. The Liberali et al. application remains conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge.
